catalog_quote: § 49. Один из слогов в слове является ударным. ... 1. В двусложных, трех- и четырехсложных корневых словах с краткими гласными ударение обычно падает на последний слог: хызыл 'красный', хузух 'орех', хузурух 'хвост', чистек 'ягода', палтырган 'дягиль', харагай 'сосна'.

new_statements.quote: § 31. [...] Demnach können auch im Koibalischen sowohl betonte als unbetonte Silben sowohl lang als kurz sein. § 32. Der Ton ruht im Koibalischen in der Regel auf der Endsilbe. Ist die Endsilbe aber kurz und die vorletzte lang, so neigt sich das Tongewicht sehr schwach auf die Endsilbe und es kommt dem Ohre fast vor, als rücke der Accent auf die vorletzte Silbe zurück. Doch ist dieses Zurückrücken nur scheinbar, denn bei einer angestrengteren Aussprache wird auch in diesem Fall die Endsilbe betont.
new_statements.translation: § 31. [...] Accordingly, in Koibal both stressed and unstressed syllables can be either long or short. § 32. In Koibal the stress as a rule rests on the final syllable. But if the final syllable is short and the penultimate long, the weight of the stress inclines only very weakly toward the final syllable, and it almost seems to the ear as if the accent moved back to the penultimate syllable. Yet this retraction is only apparent, for in a more careful pronunciation the final syllable is stressed in this case too.

new_statements.relation_note: Same placement as the catalog record (final syllable = final stress, src StressTyp2), so it agrees on placement; it adds detail the catalog lacks: stress is independent of quantity, a long penult before a short final perceptually weakens the final stress without moving it, and the stressed final syllable reduces/elides the penult vowel. The statement is about the Koibal dialect (Glottolog treats Koibal as a dialect of Khakas), not Khakas as a whole; the Karagas (= Tofa) grammar in the same volume contains no stress statement, and the Minusinsk-Tatar (Sagai/Kachin/Kyzyl/Koibal) word lists carry no stress information.
new_statements.rule_in_words: Word stress falls on the final syllable as a rule. Stress and vowel quantity are independent (stressed and unstressed syllables may each be long or short). When the final syllable is short and the penult long, the final stress is perceptually weakened and the accent seems to retract to the penult, but Castrén judges this apparent only: under careful pronunciation the final syllable is still stressed. § 33 (p. 10-11) adds that the stressed final syllable, especially when long, shortens or even elides the vowel of the penult (e.g. bîdä ~ bidä 'sister', berâi ~ brai 'all', berô ~ brô 'debt').
new_statements.exceptions: Only the perceptual near-retraction to a long penult before a short final syllable (§ 32), which the author explicitly calls illusory ('nur scheinbar'). No lexical or morphological exceptions listed. § 31 warns that accent and quantity are 'meist sehr unbestimmt' (mostly rather indeterminate) in languages without foot-based verse, Koibal included. Schiefner's preface (p. xvii, scan page 24) notes that fluctuations in vowel-quantity notation in Castrén's texts may stem from stressed syllables having been perceived as long.
new_statements.identity_note: Castrén's grammar describes the Koibal dialect (Koibalisch), recorded during his 1847 fieldwork in the Minusinsk district; Glottolog lists Koibal (koib1240) as a dialect of Khakas (khak1248) (identity from general knowledge of Glottolog; no languoid table was found inside the permitted trees to re-verify the code). The same volume's Karagas grammar concerns Karagas = Tofa (a distinct Sayan Turkic language, Glottolog tofa1245), and its accent chapter says nothing about Karagas stress; the appended word lists cover the 'Tatar dialects of the Minusinsk district' (Sagai, Kachin, Kyzyl, Koibal, i.e. Khakas varieties) plus Soyot, but carry no stress statement. The stress statement therefore applies to one Khakas dialect, Koibal, as of the 1840s.

sources.quote: §24: 'Ударение в слове экспираторное, фиксированное на последнем слоге. В многосложных словах — двухполюсное, т. е. состоит, как правило, из слабого на одном из первых слогов и сильного — на последнем слоге, напр.: пабàзынáң «от своего отца».' Exceptions listed: in negative verb forms main stress stays on the last stem syllable before the negation affix (чобáлбазаң); full person affixes do not take stress (пàр-ғáй-бын); present -ча (< чат-) unstressed (пáрча); enclitics (àлáй-ох); 'в сагайском диалекте ударение иногда может перейти на первый слог и в коренных словах: áғыс (вм. ағáс)'. §25: phr

sources.quote: No statement on stress position. Instrumental summary: in Khakas bisyllables V-CVC with a wide V1 and narrow V2 separated by a voiced/sonorant C, first-syllable vowels exceed final vowels in duration by 1.5-3.1x, reaching the duration of contracted long vowels; no lengthening before geminate/voiceless C. Relevant only as a caveat that duration is not a clean cue to the final stress the grammars describe.
